LESSON: WRITING 4.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: CONNECTORS OF SEQUENCE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.5: Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can a good paragraph be developed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify connectors of sequence from a given text
2. sequence ideas in a given paragraph
3. appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 4.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: CONNECTORS OF SEQUENCE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 4.5.1 PARAGRAPHING: CONNECTORS OF SEQUENCE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify connectors of sequence from a given text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify connectors of sequence from a given text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify connectors of sequence from a given text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify connectors of sequence from a given text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Sequence ideas in a given paragraph

What this means
In this part you learn to sequence ideas in a given paragraph. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sequence ideas in a given paragraph.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sequence ideas in a given paragraph. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify connectors of sequence from a given text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence to a partner. (skill: sequence ideas in a given paragraph)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify connectors of sequence from a given text.
3. Practise this skill: sequence ideas in a given paragraph.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of idea connectors for clarity in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can a good paragraph be developed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 4.5.1 Paragraphing: Connectors of sequence means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify connectors of sequence from a given text.
5. Be able to: sequence ideas in a given paragraph.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
